description: Combustión Espontánea is an interdisciplinary team bringing together expertise in lunar topography, orbital mechanics, physics validation, power systems engineering, and 3D web visualization. We share a passion for bridging the gap between raw planetary science datasets and agile, intuitive decision-making tools for sustainable exploration of the Moon's South Pole.
summary:
At the Moon’s South Pole, the Sun never rises more than a few degrees above the horizon. A landing just kilometers off-target can mean permanent shadow — no solar power, no direct communication with Earth. For NASA’s CLPS missions targeting the South Pole, choosing the right landing site is one of the most consequential decisions in the mission.

KillaLand is an interactive, browser-based platform that makes this decision visible. It processes real NASA data — LOLA elevation models and JPL Horizons ephemerides — to compute solar exposure, terrain slope, permanent shadow, and Earth line-of-sight for 12 candidate landing sites, rendered live on a 3D lunar globe.

The platform offers two modes: Professional Mode for mission planners needing quantitative metrics, and Student Mode for anyone curious about lunar science. No installation. No login. Open in a browser — right now.

KillaLand prepares humanity to open the doors to the Moon.
details:
KillaLand solves a real mission-critical problem: at the Moon’s South Pole, the Sun never rises more than a few degrees above the horizon. A landing site just a few kilometers off can mean permanent shadow — no solar power, no direct contact with Earth. Yet most tools that analyze this either require specialized software or bury the data behind complex interfaces.

We built KillaLand as a fully browser-based 3D platform that lets anyone evaluate candidate CLPS landing sites in real time, using actual NASA data — no installation, no login.

How it works:
The app loads JPL Horizons ephemeris data and LOLA elevation models for 12 South Pole candidate sites. For any selected site, it computes terrain slope, solar exposure windows, permanent shadow fraction, and Earth line-of-sight — all rendered live on a 3D lunar globe with a local terrain patch and a first-person surface view.

Two modes for two audiences:

  • Professional Mode — raw metrics, mission-window analysis, slope maps, full parameter control
  • Student Mode — plain-language labels, preset scenarios, guided tooltips; same data, simpler interface

Tech stack: React 19 · TypeScript · Three.js 0.187 · @react-three/fiber · Zustand · Tailwind CSS 4 · Vite 8 — 42 automated tests, all passing.

Impact: KillaLand makes NASA’s open lunar data accessible to mission planners, STEM educators, and the next generation of space explorers.
